messages:
kai: Heads-up — I'm proposing a change to admission control for bursty low-priority workloads. Current behaviour queues everything up to N=500 and blocks hot-paths. Thinking we should: 1) fast-reject if queue > 300 for low-priority class; 2) degrade to CPU/quantized small-model path for best-effort requests instead of queuing; 3) keep a small short queue (50) for mid-priority to absorb microbursts. Rationale: tail latency spikes and OOMs on GPU pools when queue grows >300.

maria: +1 on the rationale, we've seen p99 blow up during promo traffic. quick q: how do we detect "low-priority" reliably? request metadata? token budget?

kai: We'll use route tags + client tier. Default low-priority = unauthenticated / best_effort tag or explicit header `x-rw-priority: low`. Also allow rate-limit fallback for anonymous requests.

aj: Curious about degrade path — are we spinning up CPU inference in the same cluster or routing out to the smaller quantized variant? Cost tradeoffs matter.

kai: Plan is to route to a pre-provisioned fleet of CPU/quantized nodes (small models) in the same region. Config snippet below: 
```
admission: 
  policies: 
    - name: fast_reject_low
      when: queue_length > 300 and priority == low
      action: reject  # 429 with Retry-After
    - name: degrade_to_cpu
      when: queue_length > 100 and priority == low
      action: route_to: small-quantized-cpu
      quota: 200qps
    - name: short_buffer_mid
      when: priority == mid and queue_length < 50
      action: queue
```

lex: two operational concerns: 1) customer expectations for Dedicated — customers may expect no rejects; 2) telemetry — we need tagging for UI so console shows counts of rejects vs degradations.

kai: Great callouts. For Dedicated we'll make this policy disabled by default and opt-in via tenant config. For hosted customers, low-priority is only applied to unauthenticated and free-tier. We'll emit metrics: `admit.reject.count`, `admit.degrade.count`, `admit.queue.length` with labels `region, pool, priority`.

nora: Also add a soft-fallback: if degrade path latency exceeds X ms, then we should start returning 503 (fail-open?) or fallback to streaming partial result. We saw CPU path occasionally get backpressured and then everything stalls.

kai: Good — propose a small SLA guard: if degrade_p99 > 2s and degrade_error_rate > 5% for 1m window, stop degrading and start rejecting to avoid cascading.

maria: Testing plan? we should A/B with user-facing traffic and synthetic load. Canary in us-west-2 with 5% traffic for 24h. Monitor p50/p95/p99, error rates, cost delta.

aj: I can set up the traffic generator and synthetic traces. Suggest we also run a fairness sim to ensure high qps clients don't get starved.

kai: I'll open an experiment config and feature flag. Proposed rollout steps:
- stage: deployment to canary GA nodes (degrade route + metric hooks)
- canary: enable for 5% traffic, monitor 24h
- ramp: 25% for 6h if no regressions
- global: 100% for unauthenticated after 48h stability

lex: Add a communication plan: Support + Billing need a note. For Dedicated tenants we should email CSMs if any opt-ins are flipped.

maria: ops playbook for when rejects spike:
1) auto-disable fast_reject_low via FF if reject_rate > 1% for >5m
2) scale up cpu-degrade pool by factor 2 automatically instead of switching immediately
3) run snapshot tracer to capture inflight requests for debugging

sre-bot: incident-checklist: admission_policy_change detected at 1761505123, config: fast_reject_low enabled on canary.

nora: quick question about observability — will traces include which action happened? (queued, rejected, degraded)

kai: Yes, we'll add `admission.action` tag on spans and expose a Console panel showing action breakdown per route. Also add a short query for PagerDuty: `sum(admit.reject.count) by region > 50` to trigger P1 if widespread.

aj: One more: what about fairness across regions? If we redirect to CPU in same region, some regions have smaller CPU pools. We should include capacity-aware routing.

kai: plan: action routing respects `region_capacity_ratio`, prefer same-region, else cross-region to nearest with spare capacity. We'll add a safeguard to avoid cross-region for Dedicated unless tenant allows.

maria: I'm +1 on moving forward with the canary. Can someone add the FF and the canary config? I'll draft the support note.

aj: I'll create the load test config and schedule a run tomorrow 09:00 PT.

lex: I'll draft the console card and metrics dashboard.

kai: Thanks all. I'll open PR with policy config + FF and link it here. Once PR is up, please review. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/842 (admission: canary fast-reject/degrade).
